REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.2 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.3 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.4 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.5 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.6 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.6.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.6.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath. 4. The Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) has a requirement to establish a five-year indefinite delivery indefinite quantity (ID/IQ) production contract for DT-511C and DT-592D Hydrophones and spare parts in order to replenish and maintain adequate inventory to support fleet needs. The work to be performed under the contract is for the contractor to design, document, manufacture, test, package and deliver first article and production Hydrophones that meet the performance requirements of the respective DT-511C and DT-592D Hydrophone Critical Item Performance Specification (CIPS). The contractor shall also manufacture, test, package and deliver DT-511C and DT-592 Hydrophone spare parts in accordance with the respective drawings in the Reference Baseline drawing package. The drawings are marked "DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT D - Export Controlled". Distribution is authorized to the Department of Defense (DoD) and U.S. DoD contractors only. In order to view the documents, please follow the instructions in Section L. Please contact Kerin Prairie at kerin.m.prairie.civ@us.navy.mil and Keri Gunn at keri.1.gunn.civ@us.navy.mil with any questions regarding this solicitation.

title: Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within either the city limits of Richmond, Virginia; or Henrico County, Virginia; or Chesterfield County, Virginia. Home Confinement Radius: within 100 miles of the facility.
description: Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within either the city limits of Richmond, Virginia; or Henrico County, Virginia; or Chesterfield County, Virginia. Home Confinement Radius: within 100 miles of the facility. The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the city limits of Richmond, Virginia; or Henrico County, Virginia; or Chesterfield County, Virginia. Home Confinement Radius: within 100 miles of the facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 20 beds for the base year and an estimated maximum of 40 beds (35 males and 5 females). The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum of 10 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum of 20 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC27R00000006 will be available on or about October 30, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

ACQUISISTION DESCRIPTION: 2.1: RFI: A Request for Information shall be published to https://sam.gov whereby interested architect-engineering companies shall submit an SF330 package. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.2 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.3 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.4 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.5 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.6 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.6.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.6.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath. 4. Solicitation number FA8224-27-Q-0001 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for monthly and annual inspection, maintenance, and monitoring of portable fire extinguishers, and annual fire suppression system inspection located within AMXG facilities at Hill AFB, Utah. As provided in the attached statement of work, all work on this contract shall comply with applicable federal, state, local, and Hill AFB fire prevention regulations It is the Government�s intention to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a single entity for a one-year period with four additional option years. This is a Request for SF330s for Architect/Engineer (A/E) Design Services for Project Number 578-27-003: Renovate A Section 1st Floor Bldg. 1 (AE) at the Edward J. Hines VA Hospital in Hines, IL. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO SOLICITATION PACKAGE WILL BE ISSUED via SAM.gov. A request for proposal will be issued directly to the top-rated firm for which negotiations will commence in accordance with FAR part 36. The anticipated A/E design services, to be awarded, will be procured in accordance with the Selection of Architects and Engineers Act (Public Law 92- 582), FAR Part 36.6 and VA Acquisition Regulation 836.6. Period of Performance: 449 Calendar Days Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 NAICS Code: 541310 Size Standard: $12.5 Million SBA & SAM : in accordance with VAAR 819.7003, at the time of SF330 submission and prior to award of any contract, the offeror must represent to the contracting officer that it is a (1) SDVOSB eligible firm; (2) Small business concern under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to the acquisition; and (3) SDVOSB listed as verified in SBA at: https://veterans.certify.sba.gov/ Additionally, all eligible firms must be registered and current in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be evaluated and eligible for contract award. If the firm is not registered in SAM, you may register online at https://www.sam.gov. 1. PURPOSE: This Source Selection Plan (SSP) outlines the procedures that will be used to solicit architectural and engineering (AE) design services for Project 578-27-003 Renovate A Section on First Floor of Building 1. The goal of this project is to provide complete AE design services to renovate section A of the 1st floor of building 1. 2. ACQUISISTION DESCRIPTION: 2.1: RFI: A Request for Information shall be published to https://sam.gov whereby interested architect-engineering companies shall submit an SF330 package. This competitive procurement shall utilize a best value trade-off source selection process identified in FAR 15. 2.1.a: Source Selection Evaluation Board (SSEB): For the purpose of this acquisition, the SSEB will be same as the Technical Evaluation Board (TEB). 2.1.b: Below are the individual (TEB) evaluation criteria and ratings for the SF330s, listed in descending order of importance. FACTOR 1: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL COMPETENCE (30 Maximum Points) Subfactor 1A: Specialized Experience (15 Points). Subfactor 1B: Additional Experience (10 points). Subfactor 1C: Technical Competence (5 points). The A/E Firm shall demonstrate its specialized experience and technical competence in the design and construction period services for projects of similar size and complexity. Specialized project experience should include design of renovations to existing hospitals, renovations to buildings constructed prior to 1970 w/space constraints, design of Pathology Suites, and HVAC upgrades to existing hospitals. Additional experience includes mechanical, electrical, and structural engineering, architecture, interior design and finishes, physical security upgrades, building management systems/building automation systems (BMS/BAS), Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD), critical path scheduling, fire protection, construction infection control protocols, design and installation of biological refrigeration and preservation systems, design and installation of vacuum tube transport systems, and project phasing and coordination in an active hospital setting. Offeror shall provide a minimum of three (3), and no more than five (5) recent and relevant Government and private experience projects similar in size, scope, and complexity, and experience with the type of projects/competence above. Relevant is defined as those task requirements identified in the Statement of Work. Recent is defined as services provided within the past seven (7) years with at least 50% of the Construction completed. At a minimum, include the following for each submitted project (if applicable): Project title, location, contract number, and detailed narrative describing the scope of services provided including the type of work performed by the offeror and its role in the project i.e., prime contract, Teaming Partner, or subcontractor. Project Owner, owner s point of contact including telephone number and email address. Services & Deliverables provided under the contract/task order Period of Performance, including start and completion dates for design and construction if applicable. Estimated cost of construction based on AE s design Final construction cost (or projected final construction cost if still underway) The percentage of total cost resulting from changes due to AE omissions. To demonstrate technical competence, the offeror shall include narratives of how the firm addresses each of the following topics. Simply restating this list will not be sufficient. The management approach The coordination of disciplines and subcontractors Quality control procedures Familiarity with VA Design Guides/Manuals, Master Specifications and other applicable standards. FACTOR 2: PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATIONS (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 2A: Key Positions (15 Points). Subfactor 2B: SDVOSB Compliance (5 Points). The architects and engineers on the firm s staff representing the project or signing/stamping drawings in each discipline must possess a minimum of five (5) years of experience and are required to be licensed, registered, or certified by a U.S. state, the District of Columbia, or a U.S. territory. Provide professional license jurisdiction of issue and license numbers and/or proof of licensure. A resume for each of these key positions must be provided, corresponding with the title matching the disciplines listed for the project. At a minimum, the offeror must describe the professional qualifications and specific experience in the required disciplines within the past five (5) years. Key positions and disciplines required for this project include, but are not limited to: Project Manager Architect Mechanical Engineer Electrical Engineer Plumbing Engineer Structural Engineer Interior Designer The evaluation will consider education, certifications, training, registration, overall and relevant experience and longevity with the firm. Offer must include the following statement of SDVOSB compliance when submitting the personnel proposed to perform the work under this requirement: I [signatory authority] ______________________, [company] _____________________; certify that the team proposed to perform under this requirement demonstrates the capability of 50% SDVOSB performance in compliance of 48 CFR 852.219-10. FACTOR 3: PAST PERFORMANCE (20 Maximum Points) Subfactor 3A: Past Performance of projects identified in FACTOR 1. (15 Points). Subfactor 3B: Average Past Performance of all projects (5 Points). Provide CPARS data for all projects identified in FACTOR 1. For any project that does NOT have CPARS data available, a Past Performance Questionnaire (PPQ) is required to be submitted with the SF330. Please utilize the attached PPQ document. CPARS data and PPQs will not be included in the page count. All projects provided in the SF330 must be completed by the office/ branch/ individual team member performing the work under this contract. title: Y--NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice: NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant PURPOSE: The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Upper Colorado Basin Region, Four Corners Construction Office (FCCO), is issuing this pre-solicitation notice for a contemplated construction project titled: Navajo Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant. This requirement is being procured in accordance with Part 14 of the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) with a set-aside for small businesses. The Bureau of Reclamation intends to issue a competitive solicitation for this requirement. Based on market research it was determined that there were a sufficient number of qualified small businesses with sufficient bonding capacity to perform as the prime contractor on this project, and as such, it is anticipated to be set-aside for small businesses. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Navajo Gallup Water Supply Project (NGWSP) is a major infrastructure project that once constructed, will convey a reliable municipal and industrial water supply from the San Juan River to the eastern section of the Navajo Nation, southwestern portion of the Jicarilla Apache Nation, and the city of Gallup, New Mexico via approximately 280 miles of pipeline, several pumping plants, and two water treatment plants. The principal components of work for the Cutter Lateral Reach 21 Booster Plant include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Pre-engineered concrete booster pump station, concrete foundation pad, pipe encasement, yard pipe, fencing, electrical equipment, gravel surfacing, and pipe connections. 2. Installation of secondary regulation tank at Regulation Tank No. 3 site, foundation, electrical equipment, yard pipe, and pipe connections. 3. Erosion and scour restoration/prevention: a. Includes a retaining wall, swale, runoff channel, and site regrading. 4. Reinstallation of gravel surfacing at Regulation Tank No. 3 site. 5. Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) equipment and radio communications system. LOCATION OF THE WORK: The NGWSP Cutter Lateral Reach 21 booster plant is located approximately 26 miles South of Bloomfield, NM off County Road 7575 near U.S. Highway 550, at the base of Huerfano Mesa in San Juan County, New Mexico. NAICS AND SIZE STANDARD: The NAICS code for this project is 237110 (Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction) with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. COMPETITION: Solicitation 140R4026B0003 is anticipated to be conducted as a small business set-aside. The project specifications and project location will be defined in the solicitation document. The solicitation will require a bid guarantee of at least 20% of the bid price. The Contract will require payment and performance bonds for 100% of the contract price. Offerors must have sufficient bonding capacity. DISCLOSURE OF THE MAGNITUDE OF THE CONSTRUCTION PROJECT: The magnitude of this project is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. SOLICITATION RELEASE DATE: All responsible sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A free, electronic copy of the solicitation will be available on APPROXIMATELY November 2, 2026, at https://www.sam.gov/. Simply type in solicitation number "140R4026B0003" in the Keyword / Solicitation # field. A draft solicitation for comment has been attached to this announcement. The purpose of the draft solicitation is for comments only. When comments are received and incorporated, the solicitation will be posted requesting the submission of proposals. This project will follow a best-value procurement process under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 14. Questions and comments must be submitted in writing by e-mail to Philoma Singer at philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov and Tyler Spencer, at tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM, www.sam.gov): The System for Award Management (SAM) is a recently implemented Federal Government owned-and-operated FREE web site that consolidates the capabilities in Central Contractor Registration (CCR)/Federal Register (FedReg), Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA), and Excluded Parties List System (EPLS). Offerors must be successfully registered in SAM in order to be considered for a government contract award. If you had an active record in CCR, you have an active record in SAM. SITE VISIT: The Government intends to conduct a site visit for highly interested vendors AROUND November 12, 2026. Information regarding the site visit will be in Section L of the solicitation once released. POINT-OF-CONTACT FOR QUESTIONS: The Contract Specialist for this solicitation is Philoma Singer at philoma_singer@ios.doi.gov. The Contracting Officer for this solicitation is Tyler Spencer, tyler_spencer@ios.doi.gov. Any communication regarding this procurement must be made in writing and forwarded via email and must identify the solicitation number, company name, address, email address, phone number including area code, and point of contact. Emails shall be addressed to the Contract Specialist and cc the Contracting Officer. NOTE: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (SOLICITATION), AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), NOR IS IT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). It is not to be construed as a commitment by the requesting party to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals, bids, or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this Notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this Notice. This FedBizOps Notice is strictly for compliance with FAR Subpart 5.2. As a result of this Notice, the Government may issue a competitive solicitation; however, should such requirements materialize, no basis for claims against the Government shall arise as a result of a response to the Notice (e.g. use of such information as either part of its evaluation process or in developing specifications for any subsequent requirement). THE CURRENT SOLICITATION NUMBER 140R4026B0003 (A FISCAL YEAR 2026 SOLICITATION NUMBER) WILL BE UPDATED AFTER OCTOBER 10, 2026, TO A FISCAL YEAR 2027 SOLICITATION NUMBER. SOLICITATION IS EXPECTED TO BE ISSUED IN EARLY NOVEMBER 2026. THIS IS A RESULT OF GOVERNMENT SYSTEM LIMITATIONS. AN ADDENDUM WILL BE ISSUED TO THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE WITH THE NEW SOLICITATION NUMBER.

description: **********THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY********** Solicitations are not available at this time. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. The information gathered from the market research questionnaire will be vital in the formation and set aside status of the solicitation. The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Field Acquisition Office, Grand Prairie, Texas, intends to make a single award to a responsible entity for the provision of Mobile Diagnostic Services to the inmate population at the Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Miami located at 15801 S.W. 137th Avenue, Miami, FL 33177. The contract period will consist of a base period from date of award through 12 months, with four (4) one-year option periods. The North American Industrial Classification (NAICS) code is 621512 - Diagnostic Imaging Centers, (Size Standard of $19 Million). General Information regarding the BOP is located at www.bop.gov. Mobile Diagnostic Services to include but not limited to: CT scan, MRI, Sleep Disorder, Ultrasound/Echo, Nerve Conduction test, Mammograms, Holter Monitor, Nuclear testing, Thallium Stress test, Simple Stress test, Pet Scans, Bone and Joint Scans, Fluoroscopy test, Bone Densitometer, Pulmonary Function test, and Intravenous Pyelograms (IVP)/Urography test. Providers shall render such services in compliance with applicable statutes regulations and rules of federal, state, and other governmental bodies having jurisdiction over the Facility, including but not limited to, AHCA and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA); the reasonable policies, rules, and regulations of the Facility; the standards of The Joint Commission (JC); and currently accepted and approved methods and practices. The Contractor will also provide written results and interpretation of the executed procedure within 24 hours for STAT requests and within 4-5 days for routine requests. All contractors doing business with the Federal Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. The website for registration is www.sam.gov. If you have questions about the System for Award Management (SAM), Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your quote, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org.

title: P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida - AMAG Access Control Equipment panel
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southeast (NAVFAC SE) is performing a market survey to determine if other potential sources of supply can provide an access control equipment panels that has equal performance and that can fully integrate with the existing AMAG Symmetry Enterprise video surveillance system as the AMAG M2150-2DBC, M2150-4DBC, M2150-DBU/MKII, and M2150-8DBC/MKII manufactured by AMAG Technology, 2205 W. 126th Street Unit B, Hawthorne, CA 90250. Fiscal Year 2027 PROJECT P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida, requires the following characteristics. Provide access control equipment panel with the following capabilities: Must fully integrate into the existing AMAG Symmetry Enterprise access control system to include all software, hardware, database, and licensing. Connects to AMAG Symmetry management software via LAN Can control up to 16 doors per equipment panel Can manage 20,000 card holders and 65,000 offline transactions (expandable to 250,000) Connect smart card, proximity readers Wiegand support using WIM UL 294 and UL 1076 listed 100 Mbps network connection Input and output modules This notification is for market research purposes only to identify if other potential sources of supply can meet the requirements of the Government. title: B-21 Field Training Detachment Facility, Dyess AFB-OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI �B-21 Field Training Detachment Facility, Dyess AFB DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION This project will construct a two-story, approximately 55,617 gross square foot Field Training Detachment facility for B-21 maintenance training at Dyess Air Force Base, Texas, with an estimated Construction Cost Limitation (CCL) of $66,200,000. The facility will feature a steel-frame structure with a metal roof, concrete masonry unit exterior walls, and a drilled concrete pier foundation system designed for local expansive soil conditions. Functional requirements include high bay trainers and classrooms for B-21 maintenance, substantial secure space constructed in compliance with Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705 standards with construction security surveillance, a 440-ton HVAC capacity, ducted communications, utilities, and associated site infrastructure and paving. INSTRUCTIONS TO INDUSTRY Review Attached Project Information Packet (PIP): Interested firms are directed to review the attached document. This packet provides comprehensive project requirements, constraints, and the complete questionnaire reference. Submit Responses via Microsoft Forms: To streamline the collection and analysis of industry feedback, responses to the market research questionnaire must be submitted electronically via the following link: Online Feedback Form: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/bTXNv35d0c Response Due Date: All electronic responses must be submitted via the online form no later than October 27, 2026, at 2:00 PM Central Time (CT). The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics, Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) is to support our Nation�s Veterans by providing acquisition and logistics solutions for VA. In meeting these goals, TAC is responsible for preparing and executing quality contracts that support the Information Technology (IT) efforts and needs of its customers across VA, which enables our customers to provide best value solutions to Veterans and their families. TAC employees are forward-thinking, smart, and innovative acquisition professionals, with strong technical and leadership competencies. To continue to offer our customers customized and responsive service, maintain nimble operations, and provide expert technical support services, TAC must ensure its workforce continues to enhance and maintain knowledge and awareness across a variety of current and emerging IT technologies and trends. The TAC seeks to expand workforce awareness and readiness for Robotic Process Automation (RPA). This training shall be for up to three-days, predominantly informational and demonstration-driven course provides foundational understanding of RPA, VA-aligned use cases, and a limited hands-on component to reinforce learning. 2.0 TRAINING REQUIREMENTS The TAC has a requirement for RPA training to be delivered to its workforce. Facilitation � All training courses shall be �live,� virtual, instructor led training delivered in real-time and not pre-recorded or self-paced. Schedule � All training shall be delivered in Fiscal Year 2025 between October 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. No training is permitted during 4th quarter of the Fiscal Year. The Contractor is responsible for coordinating a final training schedule in accordance with the requirements in this notice for approval by the Government within two (2) weeks of the training start date. Course Content � Contractors shall effectively utilize demos, knowledge checks, and hands-on learning activities as appropriate. The training courses shall include up-to-date training material on the latest versions of the latest products. Students should be provided with or have access to view, listen, and/or print all course content. Course content shall be available online to students in video, audio and/or written transcript formats. Changes � The Contractor shall accommodate student changes within 24-hours of the start of any training class session. Changes include student drop-out, student additions, and student switches. It does not include additional students beyond the stated student maximums. Technical Support � The Contractor shall be always available during the course. Section 508 � The training shall meet Section 508 compliance standards TRAINING DELIVERABLES All deliverables shall be in a standardized format. Kick-off Meeting and Course Schedule (Deliverable 1) The Contractor shall conduct a kick-off meeting within one (1) week of contract award with the Government POCs. The Contractor shall coordinate a final course schedule for approval by the Government. The Contractor shall coordinate a final Training Schedule with draft course curriculum in accordance with the requirements of this PWS for approval by the Government. 2. Welcome Letter / Course Curriculum and Training Materials (Deliverable 2) The Contractor shall provide the Course Curriculum and Training Materials to the Government POCs no later than two weeks prior to the scheduled start date of the training course. The Course Curriculum and Training Materials shall include the course agenda, learning objectives, presentation materials, and materials for practical exercises, case studies, and job aids, as applicable. The Contractor shall be responsible for coordinating with the Government point of contract (POC) to release a welcome letter and virtual training invites to all attendees within three (3) days prior to the start of the training. 3. Attendee Roster (Deliverable 3) The Contractor shall take attendance for each training course and provide an attendance sheet to the Government delivery POCs. The attendee roster shall include the name, email, and timestamps of the attendees. Training that is multi-day shall have attendance taken each day. Training course attendance is estimated to be 20- 25 students per class. 4. Certificate of Completion (Deliverable 4) The Contractor shall coordinate with the designated Government POC for Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) approval with all awarded training. Training that extends for a working day (including lunch and breaks) shall be 8 CLPs per full day. The Contractor shall email a certificate of completion to each student within one (1) week of course completion. Certificates of Completion shall include, at a minimum, the name of the training course, training date(s), instructor, Contractor�s name, student�s name, and number of CLPs earned. 5. Feedback Survey (Deliverable 5) The Contractor shall collect training feedback from attendees upon completion of each training course. Feedback shall be provided to the Government delivery POC within three (3) weeks of the training course completion. Feedback information shall be organized and clearly presented. 3.0 SPECIFIC TASKS 3.1 INFORMATIONAL FOUNDATIONS & CONCEPTUAL UNDERSTANDING The Contractor shall deliver an instructor-led session introducing RPA fundamentals, VA use cases, and automation value. Tasks � Explain what RPA is, how bots follow rules, and how automation aligns with VA mission needs. � Demonstrate VA-aligned RPA workflows to build conceptual understanding. � Introduce core criteria for automation suitability (rules-based, repetitive, high-volume). � Discuss VA Tools for RPA such as UiPath, Blue Prism, and the use of VA RPA Platform. Deliverables Presentation deck Demonstration scripts and recordings 3.2 DEMONSTRATION-DRIVEN WORKFLOW DEEP-DIVE The Contractor shall conduct demo-intensive instruction deep-diving into RPA workflow design and operations. Tasks � Demonstrate step-by-step bot logic (triggers, rules, decisions, exception handling, audit logging). � Show operational dashboards for monitoring and orchestrating workflows. � Provide narrated, multi-step RPA workflow walk-throughs relevant to VA operations. Deliverables Bot Suitability Evaluation Guide VA-aligned suitability checklist 3.3.2 BRAINSTORMING SESSION (TALK, DEMO, GROUP EXERCISE) Conduct a structured session to identify RPA opportunities. � Talk: Explain problem identification, workflow pain-points, and target improvements. � Demo: Decompose a VA process into discrete steps and map to automation criteria; present impact-effort examples. � Group Exercise: Small groups brainstorm tasks, define current and target states, validate against suitability criteria. title: Intent to Sole Source - Lunar Exploration Ground Sites (LEGS) Public Private Partnership (PPP)
description: NASA Glenn Research Center (GRC) has a requirement for Lunar Exploration Ground Sites (LEGS) Public Private Partnership (PPP). NASA GRC intends to award a sole source contract to KSAT Inc. under the authority of FAR 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements to develop a global network of Lunar Exploration Ground Sites (LEGS) under a Public Private Partnership (PPP) model. LEGS will provide high-availability, direct-to-Earth communications coverage for spacecraft operating between 36,000 kilometers and 2 million kilometers from Earth, increasing NASA�s capacity to send and receive lunar data. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Ian Park, Contracting Officer at HQ-SCaN-LEGS@mail.nasa.gov no later than 3:00PM ET on 30OCT26. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at : https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

title: Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Philadelphia District, intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Preventative Maintenance and Repair of Heavy Equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office within the USACE Philadelphia (NAP) District area of responsibility in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor is responsible for scheduling work in accordance with the requirements of task order issued and during regular business hours when scheduling on site work. The site conducts regular business from 7:00am to 3:00pm, Monday through Friday, except for federal holidays. All work is to be performed during these regular business hours. Any hours to be worked outside of the regular business hours shall be coordinated with the COR. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform preventative maintenance and repair of heavy equipment for the Fort Mifflin Project Office as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. The contractor shall perform to the standards in this contract. The Fort Mifflin Project Office is responsible for the construction of the district�s disposal areas located along the Delaware River. Our mission supports the deepening and the maintenance dredging of the Delaware River and Wilmington Harbor. Heavy Equipment is utilized to construct dikes, ditching for drying and other dirt work. Our equipment is currently composed of D6 Dozers, Excavators (tracks and pontoons), dump trucks (articulated). Without equipment to provide the necessary dirt work in these disposals� areas, dredging assignments in the Delaware Harbor could not be accomplished. It is important that dredging and proper disposal activities of dredge materials is accomplished because it directly effects commerce and the safety of vessels transporting commodities and other resources to the ports. See attachment labeled "W912BU26QA024_FMPO Combined Solicitation Synopsis.pdf" with the requirements of this RFQ and other attachments required for informational and submission purposes.

title: P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida - Accurate Lock & Hardware
description: Notice of intent to use a brand name product. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Southeast (NAVFAC SE) is performing a market survey to determine if other potential sources of supply can provide a ligature-resistant sliding door system that has equal performance to the LR-SDS / SL-LR-SDS, manufactured by Accurate Lock & Hardware, 1 Annie Place, Stamford, CT 06902. Fiscal Year 2027 PROJECT P7777 ACC SARP Replacement NAS Jacksonville, Florida, requires the following characteristics. Provide ligature-resistant sliding door system with the following capabilities: Ligature-Resistant Design � A sliding door system specifically designed for behavioral health environments that eliminates ligature opportunities associated with conventional swinging doors, including the top edge of the door and side latch locations. The system shall utilize a concealed overhead track, concealed locking hardware, ligature-resistant operating trim, and concealed vertical rod locking or latching mechanisms with no exposed anchor points or accessible cavities. Threshold and Floor Guide � An anti-barricade floor guide that allows sliding operation without creating additional ligature points. Optional threshold/transom assemblies shall be available to reduce the bottom door gap while allowing emergency access and maintaining safe operation. Safety and Security Features � The system shall reduce opportunities for patient barricading, prevent the door from being used as a swinging weapon, and provide staff override capability for all interior locking functions. Locking functions shall include behavioral health applications such as classroom, storeroom, and self-latching patient room configurations. Performance Requirements � The system shall: Meet or exceed a 150 ft-lb impact test in accordance with ANSI A250.13-2014, Section 6.1.1.2. Continue to function following impact testing. Utilize dual ball-bearing carrier assemblies rated at 1,240 lbs dynamic load capacity each. Where required, comply with ANSI/UL 1784 air leakage testing with measured leakage substantially below the allowable code limit. Unique Product Characteristics � The system incorporates proprietary concealed track, locking, and staff-override hardware specifically developed for behavioral healthcare applications. The integrated design combines ligature resistance, anti-barricade functionality, smoke-control capability (where required), and behavioral health locking functions within a single system. The LR-SDS has also been evaluated by the New York State Office of Mental Health and is included in the OMH Patient Safety Guidelines. This notification is for market research purposes only to identify if other potential sources of supply can meet the requirements of the Government. This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify other potential sources of this product. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your manufactured product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit company brochures. Please limit your submissions to five (5) one-sided pages, not including the cover or table of contents pages. In addition, Attachment 1 must be included with your submission, and does not count against the page limit. Please submit complete information via electronic mail to Reuben Amarh reuben.a.amarh.civ@us.navy.mil and Jeff Rhein at jeffrey.j.rhein.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 30 OCT 2026 at 3:00 PM ET. Any information received after the due date/time will not be considered. Any information provided to the Government in response to this RFI will become U.S. Government property. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately.

description: The Army Contracting Command � Redstone Arsenal is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a means of conducting market research to identify manufacturing capacity and capability for production of Precision Strike Missile Increment 1 (PrSM Inc 1) follow-on production contract to support the Strategic and Operational Rockets and Missiles (STORM) Project Office. DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential firms capable of providing the supplies described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition. The purpose of this source sought notice is to conduct market research to identify potential sources with capacity and capability to produce the PrSM Inc 1 missile and pod. Provide CAGE code that verifies SECRET status and submit requests for access through the SAM.GOV website. Security � Provide encrypted communications, multi-factor authentication, and a secure user role management program. Interface Dashboard � Provide facility managers with a centralized interface that flags active security risks, system vulnerabilities, and actionable mitigation guidance. Integration with Existing System � Provide seamless connectivity to the existing Johnson Control Metasys system currently serving the main hospital (Bldg 2080) at NAS Jacksonville. Seamless connectivity ensures all monitored and controlled points at the building are fully visible and accessible by the Metasys control system serving the main hospital. This notification is for market research purposes only to identify if other potential sources of supply can meet the requirements of the Government. This is not a request for proposals, quotes, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify other potential sources of this product. To be considered, please submit detailed technical data for the Government to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of your manufactured product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), a response to this notice is not an offer and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The responder is solely responsible for the information it submits and any associated costs. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. title: Data at Rest (DaR) - 400 Obsolescence Resolution
description: OBJECTIVE: The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements. SCOPE: To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DETAILS: 1. AFLCMC/WIW is requesting information from industry as part of market research to determine interest level and size of qualified vendors. 2. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. It is not a Request for Proposal, a Request for Quotation, an Invitation for Bid, a solicitation, or an indication the US Air Force (AF) or AFLCMC/WIW will contract for the items contained in the sources sought. AFLCMC/WIW will not pay respondents for information provided in response to the sources sought. 3. The Government is requesting information from vendors of all business sizes including socioeconomic programs such as 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Women Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) that are interested in performing this requirement. The Government requests interested parties submit a brief description of their company�s business size (i.e., annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), HUBZone, or SDVOSB, Women Owned Small Business, or small business), and any anticipated teaming arrangements. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision. 4. Interested parties should submit a capabilities package, with a cover letter, that is brief and concise yet clearly demonstrates ability to meet the stated requirements with sufficiently qualified personnel. Provide qualification information (type and duration of employee experience relevant to the requirements) and the level of involvement (prime or sub-contractor) and time periods for work on similar projects. The capabilities package should clearly present evidence that the interested party is fully capable of providing the required services and as such may contain any information that the interested party feels relevant. 5. Responses should be submitted electronically, and must be no more than ten single-spaced pages, using 12-point, Times New Roman font, and minimum one-inch margins, in Microsoft Word format. Responses that only provide a company website will not be considered. 6. Responses to the sources sought are requested by 3PM, CDT, 12 October 2026. All responses shall be unclassified and reviewed to ensure consideration. All responses, correspondence, and/or questions related to this matter should be e-mailed to: E-mail: phaedra.prather@us.af.mil Phone: (405) 739-4340 Attachments: DAR 400 Follow On SOW_Sep 2026 DAR Follow-On draft CDRL_DID Package 2026

The goal of the project is to create a resilient coastal ecosystem within a highly urbanized setting that provides both ecological and social benefits. Primary project components include: Restoration of the Liberty State Park interior including approximately 46.2 acres of tidal wetland habitat, 25.0 acres of non-tidal wetland habitat, and 72.6 acres of native upland habitat. Enhancement of approximately 7.1 acres of existing non-tidal wetland (4.5 acres) and upland (2.6 acres) habitats by removing invasive flora and planting native species. Creation of park amenities to accommodate and provide public interaction with this habitat restoration project, such as trail networks, overlooks, bird blinds, viewing hills, and a restroom. The State of New Jersey, acting through the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP), is the non-Federal sponsor for this project. The magnitude of the Liberty State Park Ecosystem Restoration project is between $100,000,000 and $250,000,000. The duration of construction is anticipated to be approximately 1,686 calendar days after Notice to Proceed. Notice to Proceed is anticipated to occur approximately in October 2027. Responses to this source sought will be used by the Government to help determine whether the use of a PLA will achieve economy and efficiency in the completion of the subject project. All firms and labor unions should respond to this announcement if they are interested in performing the work for this project. PLA DEFINITION A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) SUBPART 22.503 - POLICY Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use project labor agreements in large-scale construction projects to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project (see 22.502), agencies shall require use of project labor agreements for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception at 22.504(d) applies. An agency may require the use of a project labor agreement on projects where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project, if appropriate. An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and Be consistent with law. Agencies may consider the following factors in deciding whether the use of a project labor agreement is appropriate for a construction project where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project: The project will require multiple construction contractors and/or subcontractors employing workers in multiple crafts or trades. There is a shortage of skilled labor in the region in which the construction project will be sited. Completion of the project will require an extended period of time. Project labor agreements have been used on comparable projects undertaken by Federal, State, municipal, or private entities in the geographic area of the project. A project labor agreement will promote the agency's long term program interests, such as facilitating the training of a skilled workforce to meet the agency's future construction needs. Any other factors that the agency decides are appropriate. For indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts the use of a project labor agreement may be required on an order-by-order basis rather than for the entire contract. For an order at or above $35 million an agency shall require the use of a project labor agreement unless an exception applies. See 22.504(d)(3) and 22.505(b)(3). PLA COMMENT SOLICITATION In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the construction community is invited to comment on the use of PLAs. description: The Department of Commerce (DOC), National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO) Satellite and Information Acquisition Division (SIAD) located in Silver Spring, MD, intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price contract to the University of Miami ((located at Office of Research Administration 1531 Brescia Avenue Coral Gables, FL 33146 -2403; UEI RQMFJGDTQ5V3), on the basis of other than full and open competition in support of the NOAA National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS), which provides and enables oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial satellite data, products, and applications for diverse organizations and users world-wide, and the Center for Satellite Applications and Research (STAR). STAR uses innovative science and applications to transform satellite observations of the Earth into meaningful information essential to NOAA. title: Upcoming Construction Opportunity: Land Port of Entry Highgate Springs, VT
description: THIS IS A SPECIAL NOTICE OF AN ANTICIPATED PROCUREMENT. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, is issuing this Special Notice to provide advance notification of an upcoming construction procurement for the new Land Port of Entry in Highgate Springs, Vermont. GSA had previously planned to use the Construction Manager as Constructor (CMc) delivery method. GSA now anticipates proceeding with a separate construction procurement using the Design-Bid-Build (DBB) delivery method, with construction services provided by a General Contractor (GC) at a firm fixed price. This notice is intended to inform interested industry participants of the anticipated opportunity and the planned change in delivery method, as well as to request statements from interested vendor candidates. Project Location Land Port of Entry Highgate Springs, Vermont Project Description The anticipated procurement is for construction services associated with the new Land Port of Entry in Highgate Springs, Vermont, along the United States�Canada border. The project is being undertaken by GSA to provide modern border infrastructure in support of the operational, security, and facility requirements of the Federal agencies responsible for border inspection and processing. Constructed in 1997, the existing Highgate Springs Land Port of Entry is at the northern end of U.S. Interstate 89 (I- 89), approximately 40 miles north of Burlington, Vermont, and opposite the Canadian port of entry at St. Armand/Philipsburg, Quebec. Canada is completing construction of Autoroute A-35 between Montreal and the Canada/U.S. border. Canada in coordination with Vermont�s Agency of Transportation is converting Route 133 into a multilane highway, which would link Montreal to the US border with a continuous multilane highway. When completed, traffic is estimated to increase by as much as 30% at this port of entry. The existing site occupies approximately 16.1 acres and includes seven buildings totaling approximately 44,000 gross square feet. The site is bounded to the north by the U.S./Canada border, to the east by the northbound lanes of I-89 and rock outcroppings and bluffs, to the south by the former site of the State of Vermont�s Welcome Center, and to the west by privately owned land. Lake Champlain is about 1/2 mile to the west. Tenants include the U.S. Department of Homeland Security�s Customs and Border Protection ; the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services� Food and Drug Administration; the U.S. Department of Agriculture�s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, and GSA. This project will construct a new fully operational Land Port of Entry at Highgate Springs with expanded capacity to alleviate the increase in commercial and personally owned vehicle (POV) traffic expected upon the completion of Canada�s A-35 expansion project. The project is intended to deliver a modern, functional, secure, and efficient land port of entry that supports the movement of people and goods while meeting applicable Federal facility standards, building codes and security requirements. The anticipated construction scope includes the labor, materials, equipment, supervision, coordination, and other resources necessary to complete the work in accordance with the contract documents. The final scope of work, project requirements, and construction specifications will be provided in a forthcoming solicitation. Anticipated Delivery Method Design-Bid-Build / General Contractor GSA anticipates procuring construction services through a Design-Bid-Build delivery method. Under this approach, the construction contractor will perform the work in accordance with the completed design and the requirements established in the solicitation and resulting contract at a firm-fixed price. The forthcoming solicitation will establish the acquisition strategy, contract requirements, evaluation criteria, and instructions for submitting offers. Anticipated Procurement GSA anticipates issuing a competitive solicitation for the construction phase of the Highgate Springs Land Port of Entry project. The solicitation is anticipated to be published on SAM.gov in November 2026. The anticipated schedule is subject to change. Interested firms are encouraged to monitor SAM.gov for the forthcoming solicitation and any subsequent procurement announcements. The full description of the work, construction requirements, anticipated schedule, contract terms, and proposal submission instructions will be provided in the solicitation. Vendor Response and Requested Interested vendors are requested to submit a brief statement outlining their qualifications, relevant project experience, and interest in this project to the Point of Contact listed below by October 30, 2026. This notice is not a solicitation, invitation for bids, or request for proposals. Submissions should be sent directly to the Point of Contact listed below. This notice does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation, award a contract, or proceed with the anticipated procurement. Any procurement will be conducted in accordance with the solicitation and applicable acquisition requirements. GSA will not reimburse any costs incurred by interested parties in connection with this notice. Point of Contact Questions concerning this Special Notice may be directed to: David Mazzolini Senior Contracting Officer General Services Administration, Public Buildings Service Email: david.mazzolini@gsa.gov Interested parties should refer to the forthcoming solicitation on SAM.gov for official procurement information, requirements, and instructions.

title: Europe South District Playground Inspection, Maintenance, and Repair
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is one of only two federally operated school systems in the United States. DoWEA plans, directs, coordinates, and manages pre-kindergarten through grade 12 educational programs on behalf of the Department of War (DoW). DoWEA operates approximately 165 brick-and-mortar schools across eight districts located in seven U.S. states, eleven foreign countries, Guam, and Puerto Rico, serving more than 72,000 students worldwide. DoWEA Europe consists of multiple districts encompassing schools, District Superintendent Offices (DSOs), and Student Transportation Offices (STOs) supporting children of active-duty military members and eligible civilian employees. The Contractor shall provide full-service, performance-based playground inspection, preventive maintenance, repair, emergency response, cleaning services for DoWEA facilities located in Europe South Region. For the purposes of this PWS, playgrounds include all playground systems and associated features, whether standalone or co-located, including but not limited to: Playground equipment and structures; Playground surfacing systems; Hard-surface and multi-use play courts; Outdoor recreational and athletic surfaces; and, Perimeter features, furnishings, and appurtenances. The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, tools, equipment, materials, transportation, documentation, and incidentals necessary to ensure playgrounds remain safe, serviceable, compliant, and operational throughout the period of performance.

description: Solicitation Notice: 36C79126R0011 � Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program Notice Type: Solicitation Issuance Notice Solicitation Number: 36C79126R0011 Posted Date: September 18, 2026 Response Due Date: October 19, 2026, 3:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) NAICS Code: 334510 � Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. The tiers for this procurement are as follows: Tier-1 Service?Disabled Veteran?Owned Small Business (SDVOSB): SDVOSBs shall be evaluated first in accordance with VA�s statutory obligation to prioritize verified SDVOSBs when the VA Rule of Two is met. If no award can be made at Tier-1, then verified VOSB offers will be evaluated next in Tier-2, consistent with the Veterans First hierarchy. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). Tier-3 Other Small Business Concerns: If no award can be made at Tier-3, the Government will evaluate offers from all Other-Than-Small-Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses)) in Tier 4 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101?3 and 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). PLA DEFINITION A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). FEDERAL ACQUISITION REGULATION (FAR) SUBPART 22.503 - POLICY Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use project labor agreements in large-scale construction projects to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project (see 22.502), agencies shall require use of project labor agreements for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception at 22.504(d) applies. An agency may require the use of a project labor agreement on projects where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project, if appropriate. An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and Be consistent with law. Agencies may consider the following factors in deciding whether the use of a project labor agreement is appropriate for a construction project where the total cost to the Federal Government is less than that for a large-scale construction project: The project will require multiple construction contractors and/or subcontractors employing workers in multiple crafts or trades. There is a shortage of skilled labor in the region in which the construction project will be sited. Completion of the project will require an extended period of time. Project labor agreements have been used on comparable projects undertaken by Federal, State, municipal, or private entities in the geographic area of the project. A project labor agreement will promote the agency's long term program interests, such as facilitating the training of a skilled workforce to meet the agency's future construction needs. Any other factors that the agency decides are appropriate. For indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts the use of a project labor agreement may be required on an order-by-order basis rather than for the entire contract. title: Data at Rest (DaR) - 400 Obsolescence Resolution
description: OBJECTIVE: The USAF E-3G AWACS provides worldwide response to situations requiring immediate and continuous on-scene command, control, and battle management using embedded real-time surveillance to support employment of U.S. and allied combat forces. The E-3G consists of the air vehicle, sensor systems, and computing and communications equipment. The current USAF E-3G operational fleet consists of 15 operational aircraft. The E-3G DAR-400 (part numbers 63-2824652-01 through -03) is a mission critical asset and is in critical need of obsolescence resolution to prevent mission impact. Since the DAR-400 contains encrypted MCS, MSS, IPEC and GS data, a failure would directly impact operations and data security. General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS) has notified us that the DAR-400 will not be able to support or upgrade to changing NSA requirements. SCOPE: To execute the installation and integration of the obsolescence resolution for the mission-critical E-3G DAR-400 to prevent mission impact. The provided Government-owned KG-204 based solution is compliant with current DoD and NSA mandates to replace the legacy DAR-400 equipment. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DETAILS: 1. AFLCMC/WIW is requesting information from industry as part of market research to determine interest level and size of qualified vendors. 2. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ONLY. It is not a Request for Proposal, a Request for Quotation, an Invitation for Bid, a solicitation, or an indication the US Air Force (AF) or AFLCMC/WIW will contract for the items contained in the sources sought. AFLCMC/WIW will not pay respondents for information provided in response to the sources sought. 3. The Government is requesting information from vendors of all business sizes including socioeconomic programs such as 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Women Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) that are interested in performing this requirement. The Government requests interested parties submit a brief description of their company�s business size (i.e., annual revenues and employee size), business status (i.e., 8(a), HUBZone, or SDVOSB, Women Owned Small Business, or small business), and any anticipated teaming arrangements. The Government will use this information in determining its small business set-aside decision. 4. Interested parties should submit a capabilities package, with a cover letter, that is brief and concise yet clearly demonstrates ability to meet the stated requirements with sufficiently qualified personnel. Provide qualification information (type and duration of employee experience relevant to the requirements) and the level of involvement (prime or sub-contractor) and time periods for work on similar projects. The capabilities package should clearly present evidence that the interested party is fully capable of providing the required services and as such may contain any information that the interested party feels relevant. 5. Responses should be submitted electronically, and must be no more than ten single-spaced pages, using 12-point, Times New Roman font, and minimum one-inch margins, in Microsoft Word format. Responses that only provide a company website will not be considered. 6. Responses to the sources sought are requested by 3PM, CDT, 30 October 2026. All responses shall be unclassified and reviewed to ensure consideration. All responses, correspondence, and/or questions related to this matter should be e-mailed to: E-mail: phaedra.prather@us.af.mil Phone: (405) 739-4340 Attachments: DAR 400 Follow On SOW_Sep 2026 DAR Follow-On draft CDRL_DID Package 2026
